transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (OrbitGrid Partnerships), Dr. Priya Raman (Head of Solutions), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Product), Ben Kline (Infra)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'm the ae covering partners. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Liam: hi all, liam here, partnerships at orbitgrid, excited to chat about potential marketplace and go-to-market.
[00:28] Priya: priya, head of solutions, i'll lead the pilot and success metrics.
[00:35] Marco: marco, cto, i'll be focused on infra and network.
[00:42] Ethan: ethan, se at redwood, i'll cover tech compatibility and perf.
[00:50] Maya: great. high level — we see three patterns: listing on marketplace, co-sell referral, or deeper integration where orbitgrid becomes a recommended infra partner for dedicated/private deployments. curious which you're leaning toward.
[01:10] Liam: ideally marketplace + referral to start, then expand into dedicated joint pilots. we have customers asking for turnkey gpu clusters for inference.
[01:22] Maya: makes sense. a lot of partners start marketplace-only to test demand, then do a joint pilot. on the tech side, ethan, can you run through the typical connectivity options?
[01:35] Ethan: yeah, so we support hosted, dedicated and private: hosted api is easiest (no network work), dedicated is reserved gpu pools we can run on partner infra via partner-managed nodes, and private is vpc/on-prem with a private control plane. for partner infra we typically do either vpc peering or private link or a vpn tunnel depending on network policy. sometimes partners prefer s2s vpn for initial proofs.
[02:10] Marco: for us we prefer vpc peering or direct connect equivalent — low latency is important for customers doing real-time chat. what's the typical latency delta for peered dedicated instances vs hosted?
[02:24] Ethan: good q — depends on region and SKU. with peering on the same region the added network hop is minimal, usually 5-15ms extra. major factors are instance type and batching. we can tune concurrency and batching to hit latency s-los; that's where quantization and kernel selection help.
[02:47] Ben: on the skus — what gpu types have you validated? we run A100s and H100s, plus a few 80GB variants.
[02:57] Ethan: we've tested extensively on A100 and H100. H100 gives better perf for 8k and 32k contexts but also higher cost; quantization can shrink memory footprint to allow more concurrency. we also work with 80GB and 160GB. we'll share a perf spreadsheet with recommended skus per model class.
[03:20] Pria/Priya (overlap): sorry, priya — can you repeat that quantization bit?
[03:25] Ethan: sure — sorry for jargon, quantization is lossy compression that reduces model memory and compute, we have tuned quantization profiles that balance throughput vs minimal quality drop. it's part of our redwood optimize suggestions.
[03:40] Sofia: curious about the integration flow for marketplace listing — what's required from orbitgrid's side?
[03:47] Maya: typically a listing includes a product page, sample pricing, and a basic integration test. we also need a schema for provisioning (API creds plus a service account or peered network). we provide a partner onboarding checklist.
[04:05] Liam: on billing, how does revenue share work? and can customers be billed directly by the partner?
[04:12] Maya: we support a couple models: usage-based referral (customer billed by redwood, partner gets referral fee), or partner-billed marketplace listing where partner handles billing and we provide attribution. we can share a partner pricing doc.
[04:32] Marco: security — our customers are enterprise, SOC2 is required, and we need SAML SSO + audit logs + key mgmt options. do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:44] Ethan: yes, for private deployments we integrate with KMS/HSM options and customers can bring their own key material. audit logs, RBAC, and SAML/SSO are supported in the private and dedicated modes; hosted has enterprise features for SSO and logging as well. we'll share the security packet (SOC2, ISO, compliance summary).
[05:10] Liam: perfect, send the security packet.
[05:14] Maya: noted. we'll attach the security doc link to the follow-up.
[05:18] Ethan: quick note on networking — if you do a peered dedicated deployment we sometimes recommend colocating model servers in the same availability zones to reduce cross-az latency. also prefix/KV cache can make a big difference for repeated prompts.
[05:42] Ben: KV cache — are you caching on the host or at the application layer? how does that affect memory?
[05:49] Ethan: the runtime manages KV cache in-GPU to avoid reprocessing prefixes; that increases GPU memory usage but reduces token compute. we can expose cache hit metrics via the console for tuning.
[06:05] Priya: what do you recommend as success criteria for a small pilot? we want clear pass/fail metrics.
[06:12] Maya: good point — typical pilot criteria are latency p95 under X ms for target prompt mix, throughput (reqs/sec) target, cost per thousand tokens below a threshold, and qualitative NPS/accuracy checks on a small eval set. Priya, what are you thinking?
[06:30] Priya: we'd like p95 < 300ms for short chat, and cost per 1k tokens to be competitive — we'll send sample workloads. also want a security signoff.
[06:42] Maya: sounds achievable. we'll map those to suggested SKUs and batching config.
[06:48] Liam: timeline — how long to go from initial test to a marketplace listing?
[06:54] Maya: marketplace listing can be 2-4 weeks for a basic listing + test, pilot may run 4-8 weeks depending on benchmarks and integration work. deeper private deployments take longer (6-12 weeks).
[07:08] Marco: about the deeper integration — do you support partner-managed clusters where orbitgrid provides nodes and redwood runs the control plane?
[07:16] Ethan: yes, we have models where partner hosts nodes (we call it partner-managed dedicated), we run either an agent or a lightweight control plane that schedules inference and collects metrics. we can also offer a full private control plane where you host everything.
[07:34] Ben: do you have templates/helm charts or is it custom?
[07:38] Ethan: we provide helm charts, terraform modules, and an operator for on-prem. documentation link: https://redwood.ai/docs/partner-deploy (we'll include in follow-up).
[07:52] Sofia: any constraints on the container runtime or kernel modules?
[07:55] Ethan: we use mainstream container runtimes; require nvidia drivers of recent versions and some kernel settings for gpu memory pinned pages, we'll share exact node checklist.
[08:08] Maya: switching to go-to-market — what would success look like for orbitgrid? volume, revenue, or customer logos?
[08:16] Liam: initial goal is 3 pilot customers in Q2, then convert 1 into a paid marketplace listing. also co-marketing is important for us.
[08:26] Maya: we can do co-branded case studies and joint webinars. we also have a partner portal for content and leads.
[08:34] Priya: question on model catalog — can customers pick models you verify and also run their own custom models?
[08:41] Ethan: yes, redwood supports open models from our catalog and customer-provided models, but custom models may need additional onboarding for kernel selection and quantization tuning.
[08:56] Marco: about tenancy — do you offer tenant isolation in dedicated pools? how do you guarantee noisy neighbor protection?
[09:03] Ethan: dedicated pools are isolated to tenant resource pools. we do model pinning and cgroup-level isolation to avoid noisy neighbors. plus autoscaling policies to reduce contention.
[09:16] Ben: curious about throughput tests — can we run a small benchmark on our A100s and compare with your published numbers?
[09:22] Ethan: absolutely, we can provide a benchmark harness and a small dataset. we'll coordinate a bench run and analyze results.
[09:30] Liam: on commercial terms — is there a minimum commitment for dedicated?
[09:35] Maya: typically yes, reserved capacity contracts have monthly/annual commits, but for partners we have flexible pilots and special partner SKUs to avoid high upfronts.
[09:46] Sofia: legal & procurement — what's typical on data residency and data retention?
[09:51] Ethan: data residency can be enforced with private deployments or region pinning; retention policies configurable and audit logs provided. hosted mode has retention defaults but can be adjusted for enterprise accounts.
[10:08] Maya: we should talk through compliance later — we'll attach SOC2/ISO docs.
[10:12] Marco: modern question — do you support inference for 32k models natively? some of our customers want long-context summarization.
[10:20] Ethan: yes we support long contexts, but it impacts memory and throughput. we recommend H100/160GB variants for 32k workloads and specific kernel optimizations. we'll include reference configs.
[10:36] Priya: what's the typical cost delta between 8k and 32k models?
[10:40] Ethan: roughly 2-4x depending on batch sizes and sequence lengths; we'll provide the numbers in the perf sheet.
[10:49] Liam: competitors — some customers ask us about coreweave and lambdalabs, how do you differentiate?
[10:56] Maya: redwood differentiates by a unified runtime + observability + model lifecycle tooling; we optimize for production economics, which includes caching/batching, and mechanized rollouts and evals. we also have flexible deployment modes which many infra vendors don't provide end-to-end.
[11:14] Marco: noted. any partner success stories you can share?
[11:18] Maya: yes — we'll include a short case study on a partner that used dedicated pools and hit p95 latency targets while reducing cost with prefix caching.
[11:28] Ben: ok would like technical deep dive next — can we schedule with our infra and networking team?
[11:34] Maya: yes, we'll set up a 60-90 minute SE-led deep dive next week.
[11:39] Sofia: for the pilot, do you require customer data in any particular format?
[11:43] Ethan: no strict format, but for evals having a representative prompt set and gold outputs is helpful. we'll share a sample eval harness.
[11:53] Priya: for acceptance, we'll run functional checks plus perf. also need a security review — is that a separate call?
[11:59] Maya: we can do a security review; sometimes that's a separate SOC/compliance call with security. we'll coordinate.
[12:07] Liam: are there any blockers on your side in terms of partner onboarding?
[12:10] Ethan: no blockers; we need your network diagram and sample workloads. we also need to align timelines for pilot resources.
[12:18] Maya: ok recap — next step i'll send the one-pager, onboarding checklist and security packet. ethan will share perf spreadsheet and benchmark harness. orbitgrid to send topology and workloads. we'll book technical deep dive and security call.
[12:35] Marco: sounds good. small nit — please include specific driver/kernel versions for H100s in the checklist.
[12:43] Ethan: will do.
[12:45] Liam: thanks everyone. one more question — can we co-sell in our region APAC?
[12:50] Maya: yes, we have APAC region support and can enable partner listings by region. we'll include regional pricing notes.
[12:58] Sofia: thanks — we'll follow up internally after the call.
[13:03] Maya: awesome, we'll send materials and action items. thanks all.

Notes (post-call):
- Links to include in follow-up: partner playbook (short link), perf spreadsheet template, marketplace onboarding checklist, security packet (SOC2).
- Recording: fireflies link (internal)

Transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings (Pria/ Priya spelled inconsistently earlier), some speaker overlaps, proper nouns for competitors sometimes spelled differently.
